title: Option sellers need two numbers: implied and realized volatility
summary: For the wheel, covered calls or cash-secured puts, watch implied volatility and realized volatility. When IV is above realized, sellers have an edge. Usually IV trades above realized, but sometimes it does not; then it is a bad time to sell and buying options can be better.

steps.caption: A stock path over a year. Option sellers trade against how much it moves.
Implied volatility: the market's forecast of the move, priced into the options.
Realized volatility: how much the stock actually moved recently.
When IV is above realized, the gap is positive: an edge for option sellers.
When IV falls below realized, sellers are underpaid. Buying options can be the better side.

takeaways: Track both implied and realized volatility for every name you sell.
IV above realized gives sellers an edge; IV below realized favors buyers.
IV usually trades above realized, but not always.
caveats: The speaker's metric and free Chrome extension are promotional and not verified here.
